question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=84,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =0\cdot 0.2+1\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0+0.3+0.6+0.6 \\  & =1.5,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({0}^{2}\cdot 0.2+{1}^{2}\cdot 0.3+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.3+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.2)-{1.5}^{2} \\  & =(0+0.3+1.2+1.8)-2.25 \\  & =1.05.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(1.5,\frac{1.05}{84}) \\  & ∼N(1.5,0.0125).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<1.75).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<1.75) & ≈P(Z<\frac{1.75-1.5}{\sqrt{0.0125}}) \\  & =P(Z<2.24) \\  & =Φ(2.24).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.24)=0.9875.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<1.75) & =Φ(2.24) \\  & =0.9875.\end{aligned}
$$
